name: ema_crossover_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: EMA(9) / EMA(21) crossover signals on 1-min bars in range-bound markets are reliably faded because the crossover lags the actual move by 3-5 bars, meaning late momentum chasers enter at the worst price. By fading these crossovers when the stock is in a defined range (ATR_60 < 1.5 * median ATR_60 over past week), you capture the reversion when momentum fails. The edge persists because crossover signals are still heavily used by retail technical traders in India, creating predictable late entries.
stock_filter: FnO stocks with avg daily turnover > ₹50Cr, avg intraday range > 0.8%

indicators.name: atr_60_median_week
indicators.purpose: is current range below normal (approx 1 week of 1-min bars)

long.confirmation: wait 2 bars after crossover, then enter if close > ema_21

short.confirmation: wait 2 bars after crossover, then enter if close < ema_21

exit.target: 0.3% from entry or ema_9 reverts back to pre-crossover side

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 30 min

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral; retail crossover trading slowly declining but still prevalent in India

weaknesses: In genuine breakout days, fading the crossover gets destroyed — the range filter mitigates but doesn't eliminate
The 1950-bar lookback for weekly median requires significant warmup data each morning
2-bar wait for confirmation reduces trade frequency and sometimes means the reversion already happened
prior_art: Fading EMA crossovers in range-bound conditions — contrarian take on a classic retail signal
notes: Could be improved with a machine learning classifier for range vs trending regime.
